title: Should we ban the umbrellas?
hook: A perfect predictor need not be a useful intervention.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: a model leans on umbrella sales to predict rain; banning umbrellas won't stop it.

misconception: Treating feature importance isn't causal as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: a model leans on umbrella sales to predict rain; banning umbrellas won't stop it.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Rain R is equally likely 0/1; umbrella sales U=100R and street wetness W=R. If an intervention forces umbrella sales to zero, what wet-street probability remains?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-feature-importance-isn-t-causal/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: RainR fairbinary, umbrellasU=100R, wetstreetW=R. Umbrellas perfectly predictwetstreet; doU=0 keepsP(W=1)=.5. Contrast prediction error with intervention effect0.

src/demos/probability/p100-feature-importance-isn-t-causal/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: RainR fairbinary, umbrellasU=100R, wetstreetW=R. Umbrellas perfectly predictwetstreet; doU=0 keepsP(W=1)=.5. Contrast prediction error with intervention effect0.

claims.text: Banning sales retains wet-street probability 50%; observing zero sales retains 0%. In the observational data, sales perfectly predict rain and wetness.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-feature-importance-isn-t-causal/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: RainR fairbinary, umbrellasU=100R, wetstreetW=R. Umbrellas perfectly predictwetstreet; doU=0 keepsP(W=1)=.5. Contrast prediction error with intervention effect0.

claims.text: The prediction works because rain causes both variables. Intervening on umbrella sales cuts their rain-generated assignment without removing rain’s path to wet streets. A model’s predictive feature importance does not by itself measure an intervention effect.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-feature-importance-isn-t-causal/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: RainR fairbinary, umbrellasU=100R, wetstreetW=R. Umbrellas perfectly predictwetstreet; doU=0 keepsP(W=1)=.5. Contrast prediction error with intervention effect0.

claims.text: A thermometer reading predicts fever. Changing only its displayed number does what to the underlying fever in that causal model? A downstream measurement can predict a condition without being its cause.
